profile.reading:
This building at 2725 Bilter Road in Aurora, Illinois is the third data center CyrusOne added to its original Aurora campus, and the company's own materials group it with its two neighbors as CHI1, CHI2, and CHI3. The campus's history is unusually well documented because CyrusOne was a publicly traded real estate investment trust for most of the period this campus was built, and its SEC filings record that CyrusOne acquired the original 428,000 square foot Aurora facility, now CHI1, on March 31, 2016, for approximately 131.1 million dollars including transaction costs, and that CME Group, parent of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, signed a 15 year lease for data center space in that building effective April 1, 2016, one of the anchor tenancies that shaped this campus's early identity. The same SEC disclosure notes CyrusOne acquired roughly 15 acres of adjacent land at the same time for future development. A second building, CHI2, was added to the site in 2017. This building, CHI3, was added to the site in 2023, according to later trade press describing the campus's history in the context of CyrusOne's subsequent Aurora expansion plans.

CyrusOne's current marketing page for this campus states the site totals 16 acres and 450,000 square feet of technical IT space, with 114 megawatts of total IT capacity across all three buildings, cabinet capacity up to 17 kilowatts, and 98 percent carbon free or renewable electricity. It also states Green Globe three globes certification, but attributes that certification specifically to CHI1 and CHI2, not to CHI3, so this building's own certification status is not confirmed here. No source found in this research session breaks the 450,000 square feet or 114 megawatts down building by building, so none of that campus total is assigned to CHI3 individually, and this building's own square footage, IT critical load, utility feed, standby generation, or onsite generation are not separately disclosed by CyrusOne in any source located.

CyrusOne's presence in the Aurora area has grown well beyond this three building campus since CHI3 was added. In 2024 the company announced and broke ground on a second, larger Aurora area campus, also fronting Bilter Road but extending across Interstate 88 into Kendall County, planned as two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet on 32 acres with 40 megawatts of initial IT capacity, backed by a reported 350 million dollar investment, a groundbreaking in the fall of 2024 attended by Governor JB Pritzker, Aurora Mayor Richard Irvin, and ComEd president and chief executive Gil Quiniones, and supported through the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity's data center investment tax program, with an expected opening in early 2026. Separately, in June 2024 the Yorkville Planning and Zoning Commission in neighboring Kendall County recommended rezoning roughly 230 acres from single family residential to general manufacturing for a still larger, longer horizon CyrusOne campus of up to nine two story buildings planned over 10 to 20 years, a proposal that drew stated resident concern over construction and noise. Both of those newer projects sit in the same Aurora area corridor as CHI3 and illustrate the pace of CyrusOne's regional growth, but neither is this building, and neither project's figures are attributed to CHI3 here. No Aurora Planning and Zoning Commission item specifically authorizing this building's 2023 construction was located and confirmed in this research session, a gap left open rather than guessed at.

The City of Aurora publishes Planning and Zoning Commission agendas online, but the specific CHI3 item was not identified among them here, an open gap rather than an assumed absence. The best documented local government record for CyrusOne in this corridor concerns a different, newer project. In June 2024 the Yorkville Planning and Zoning Commission in Kendall County voted unanimously to recommend a Planned Unit Development rezoning roughly 230 acres from single family residential to general manufacturing for a future CyrusOne campus, a proposal that drew stated resident concern over construction and noise, with two residential properties still sitting between the rezoned parcels at the time of that vote. profile.regional_context: CHI3 sits within a fast-growing CyrusOne and ComEd-served corridor in the Aurora, Illinois area. Beyond this three-building CHI1-3 campus, CyrusOne broke ground in fall 2024 on a second, larger Aurora-area campus also fronting Bilter Road but extending across I-88 into Kendall County (two buildings, 500,000+ sq ft, 32 acres, 40 MW initial IT capacity, $350 million investment, expected open early 2026, supported by Illinois's Data Center Investment Program tax incentives), and in June 2024 the Yorkville Planning and Zoning Commission recommended rezoning about 230 acres in Kendall County for a still larger, longer-horizon CyrusOne campus of up to nine buildings over 10 to 20 years. CyrusOne's CEO has described Chicagoland as the third-largest US data center market by demand. None of these newer projects' figures belong to CHI3, which predates the 2024 announcements.

reading.body:
CyrusOne CHI3 is the third building on a 16-acre Aurora campus that began in 2016 with the acquisition of the original 428,000 square foot facility, now CHI1, anchored by a 15-year lease from CME Group signed concurrent with that acquisition. CHI2 was added in 2017 and CHI3 in 2023, completing this three-building complex on Bilter Road just west of Chicago. No IT capacity, utility power, or standby generation figure specific to CHI3 individually has been published by the operator.

The campus as a whole holds 450,000 square feet of technical IT space and 114 MW of total IT capacity across all three buildings, according to CyrusOne's current specifications. At typical AI training densities of 40 kW per rack, this campus-wide 114 MW would support roughly 2,850 racks, though this figure is not broken out per building. CyrusOne states the site offers 98 percent carbon-free or renewable electricity and Green Globe three-globe certification, though the operator attributes that certification specifically to CHI1 and CHI2, leaving CHI3's own certification status unconfirmed.

In Illinois, CyrusOne's three-building Aurora campus ranks seventh among six facilities with published megawatt figures in the state, which together total 236 MW across 44 mapped facilities statewide. CyrusOne has since announced two larger new campuses in the same Aurora and Kendall County corridor, planned to open in 2026 and developed over longer horizons, but those separate projects postdate CHI3 and their figures do not apply to this building. No specific local authorization record for CHI3's 2023 construction was located in this research.
